firstPlayerRule: In multiplayer, whoever looks most like a goblin takes the first human bidding turn.
houseFallback: If your group cannot agree on the resemblance or prefers another approach, agree to choose randomly. This is this site’s suggested house rule.
clarifications: Give that player the first player marker. Initial vault cards are chosen and revealed simultaneously during setup; bidding then begins with the marker holder and proceeds clockwise.
With two players, reveal Glavrun’s bidding card before the human players bid. In solo play, the first player marker is unused and Glavrun also reveals a card before the human acts.
After a non-final round’s Warden Phase, pass the first player marker clockwise.

internalEvidence: Complete publisher-hosted or publisher-linked PDF retrieved; relevant setup, opening-turn, variant and edition pages read and visually inspected. Reviewed PDF pages: 4, 6, 7, 10, 11, 12. Rendered setup page 4 gives the first player marker to the most goblin-like player after simultaneous starting-card selection. Page 7's two-player Glavrun box is visually before the human bidding paragraph: Glavrun reveals first, then the marker holder begins clockwise human bidding. Page 11 removes the marker in solo and places Glavrun's first reveal before the human's turn. Page 10's gear-token tie-break concerns final scoring, while its marker rotation concerns later rounds. The credits say ©2022. The resemblance criterion does not require comparison with a particular component illustration. The resemblance criterion identifies the first human actor and does not require the game's cards or a specific illustration. Automated-opponent timing and simultaneous setup are kept explicit.
uncertainty: The subjective resemblance criterion has no stated judging method or initial-start tie-break.
